title: Load a tool holder up into a mill spindle, keys aligned, while holding the drawbar release
instruction: Load the blue tool holder into the mill spindle.
context: CNC operators and machinists load a tool holder into the spindle by hand: hold the tool release, push the holder straight up with its flange slots on the spindle's drive keys, let the release go, and check the holder hangs on the latch before letting go of it (O*NET 51-9161.00 Computer Numerically Controlled Tool Operators; 51-4041.00 Machinists). Closest board tasks: 'Load a CNC tool magazine: the face mill gets empty pockets on both sides' sets tools into pockets from above; 'Replace a blade in a quick-release holder and check it is retained' and 'Hold a stick umbrella by its handle with one hand while the other pushes the runner up until it latches open' hold a release. This one adds an upward insertion against gravity, clocked to two unequal keys, into a latch that must then carry the part's weight once both hands let go.
setup: Positions are cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left; arm bases at y +30.5 and -30.5). Table: oak top, nothing else on it. Mill, fixed, grey painted steel: column 4 x 6 x 29 cm tall (x 33 to 37, y -5 to +1); arm 2 x 6 x 7 cm (x 31 to 33, z 22 to 29); spindle head 6 x 6 x 7 cm (x 25 to 31, y -5 to +1, z 22 to 29). In the head a square bore 3.4 x 3.4 cm (x 26.3 to 29.7, y -3.7 to -0.3) runs up from the spindle face (z 22) to a ceiling at z 25.8. Two black steel drive keys hang 0.8 cm under the face, centred y -2: a wide one 1.0 (x) x 1.6 (y) at x 25.2 to 26.2, a narrow one 1.0 x 1.0 at x 29.8 to 30.8. Latch: a dark steel tongue 1.0 (x) x 1.0 (z) at x 27.5 to 28.5, z 23.8 to 24.8, its tip 1.8 cm into the bore at rest (y -2.1, just past the bore's centre line), on a rod through a 1.8 x 1.8 cm window in the head's +y wall, joined outside the head to an orange plastic release tab 1.8 (x) x 1.8 (y) x 3.0 (z) at x 27.1 to 28.9, y 1.6 to 3.4, z 24 to 27. The tab slides along y on a spring (50 N/m, 20 g, stops 0.1 cm in and 2.25 cm out); pulled 2.0 cm the tongue clears the bore. Tool holder, loose, 80 g, 11.8 cm tall: blue plastic body 2.4 x 2.4 x 7.0 cm; yellow plastic flange 5.6 x 5.6 x 1.0 cm with a key slot 1.2 cm deep cut through its thickness in each of two opposite edges, 2.2 cm wide in one and 1.4 cm wide in the other; light grey shank 2.8 x 2.8 x 3.8 cm with a notch 1.4 (across) x 1.8 (deep) x 1.4 (tall) in one side face (the one with no slot), 0.8 cm under the shank top. Keyed, the wide slot faces -x, the narrow slot +x and the notch +y. It starts upright in a dark grey cup, 4 x 4 x 0.6 cm with a 3.0 cm square pocket, centred x 24, y -13, turned a quarter turn (90 degrees clockwise seen from above) from keyed: wide slot toward +y, narrow slot toward -y, notch toward +x. Seated, the flange top meets the face and the shank top the ceiling; clearances are 3 mm a side at the bore and the wide slot, 2 mm at the narrow slot and the notch.
scoring: Judged at the end, grippers open; progress flags stay set. 1.0: the holder hangs on the latch: flange top 1 to 3 mm under the spindle face, slots on the keys (yaw within 4 degrees of keyed), tilt within 3 degrees, release tab back at rest (within 2 mm) with the tongue in the notch, holder still for 1 s. 0.5: at any time the holder was seated (flange top within 3 mm of the face, yaw within 4 degrees, tilt within 3 degrees), whatever it ends as. 0.25: at any time the shank was at least 1 cm up inside the bore (a holder turned wrong stops 8 mm short; a release let go early stops the shank 1.8 cm in). Else 0. Nothing can be pushed up into the overhead bore. Check: ruler at the side for the flange gap, top photo for the tab at rest, tug the holder to see it hangs.
reset_notes: Stand the holder back in the cup, turned a quarter turn from keyed (wide slot toward +y), and check the release tab slides freely and returns to rest. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Approximate. Mill, keys, bore, notch and holder are rigid boxes with square sections and 2 to 3 mm clearance a side; the latch is a sprung slide with no ramp, and the taper is not modelled. The simulator scores the last step without opening the grippers, so a holder held up against the face, not hanging on the tongue, scores 0.5 and never more than it would if released.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (right arm reached toward the mill, holder stayed in the cup); demo: 1.0 (right arm lifted holder into spindle while left arm held tab, both let go)
